clue.text: Rash behaviour in carriage going round Circle Line

indicators.note: the carriage word travels round the other pieces, so it encloses them

parts.note: a fly is a light horse-drawn hired carriage
a circle is drawn like the letter O

explanation.surface: Someone behaves recklessly in a railway carriage as it travels round London's Circle Line.
explanation.walkthrough: 'going round' puts FLY around O and L. The Circle Line is a London Underground route, which makes 'carriage' read as a train coach.
explanation.definitionFit: Foolishness and rash behaviour are near synonyms: a reckless act is a piece of madness.

clue.text: Free to travel, having abandoned infantry first

indicators.note: the infantry piece is placed first, before the abandoned piece

parts.note: foot soldiers are infantry, so foot means infantry
loose means abandoned or unrestrained

explanation.surface: A soldier quits his regiment to roam at will.
explanation.definitionFit: Being unattached and free to go anywhere is the idiom's sense, from the foot being unbound.

clue.text: Entertaining part of what you're doing?

definitions.meaning: a crossword entry is called this, and the solver is filling in a crossword

explanation.definitionFit: Light means easy and diverting; it is also a crossword term for an answer slot.

clue.text: Longed for study taken up after some time

indicators.note: the study piece comes after the time piece

parts.note: a year is a period of time

indicators.note: in a down clue taken up means the study word is read from bottom to top

parts.note: a den is a study, a private room for work

explanation.surface: Someone wished for a study, picked up after a period of waiting.
explanation.walkthrough: 'taken up' turns DEN into NED; 'for' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: To yearn is to long for something intensely, so the two verbs are synonyms.

clue.text: Popular champion making many American friends in sultanate

indicators.note: the many and friends pieces sit inside the sultanate word

parts.note: Oman is a sultanate on the Arabian peninsula
M is the Roman numeral for a thousand, hence many
buds is American slang for friends, short for buddies

explanation.surface: A people's advocate builds ties with lots of Americans in a Gulf state.
explanation.walkthrough: 'making' is a link; 'in' puts the many and friends pieces inside the Gulf sultanate's name, split after its first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: An ombudsman investigates complaints on behalf of the public, a champion of ordinary people.

clue.text: Slow to understand such an angle

definitions.meaning: dull-witted, not quick on the uptake
an angle between 90 and 180 degrees has this name

explanation.definitionFit: The adjective means dim-witted, and in geometry it names an angle wider than a right angle.

clue.text: Irish girl caught taxi going up for game

indicators.note: in a down clue going up means the whole run is read from bottom to top

parts.note: Tara is an Irish girl's name, after the hill of the High Kings
C is the cricket abbreviation for caught
a cab is a taxi

explanation.surface: An Irish girl hails a taxi heading uptown for a game.
explanation.walkthrough: 'going up' turns the whole run TARACCAB into BACCARAT.
explanation.definitionFit: Baccarat is a casino card game.

clue.text: Such a blameworthy action could get me tried

indicators.note: could get suggests the letters might be turned into something else by reshuffling

explanation.surface: A guilty act like that could land me in court.
explanation.walkthrough: 'could get' rearranges METRIED.
explanation.definitionFit: A demerit is a fault or a mark against someone, a reason for blame.

clue.text: One's come down to earth after a short but brilliant career

definitions.text: One's come down to earth after a short but brilliant career

parts.words: One's come down to earth after a short but brilliant career
parts.note: reads as a fallen star of show business, but describes a shooting star whose blazing flight ends on the ground

explanation.surface: A celebrity returns to normal life after brief fame.
explanation.walkthrough: 'brilliant career' suggests a meteoric rise; here it means literally glowing through the sky.
explanation.definitionFit: A body from space that blazes briefly through the atmosphere and lands is a fallen space rock.

clue.text: In US city, look over new synthetic material

indicators.note: in a down clue the look piece sits over the new piece

parts.note: NY is New York
lo is an old word meaning look

explanation.surface: In New York, someone checks over a new man-made fabric.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Nylon is a man-made polymer used for fibres, a synthetic fabric.

clue.text: So tragic. I collapsed, being totally abandoned

indicators.note: something collapsed has fallen apart, so the letters are rebuilt in a new order

explanation.surface: Someone overwhelmed by grief declares they broke down in utter abandon.
explanation.walkthrough: 'collapsed' rearranges SOTRAGICI.
explanation.definitionFit: An orgy is unrestrained revelry, so behaviour of that kind is wild and wholly unrestrained.

clue.text: Copper, possibly, encountered a sign of inexperience.-

parts.note: met means encountered
L is the learner plate on a British car driven by a novice

explanation.surface: A policeman meets a sign that he is new to the job.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Copper' reads as a police officer but means the element; 'possibly' marks it as one example.
explanation.definitionFit: Copper is one example of a chemical element of that class, as are iron and tin.

clue.text: Behave like Lady Godiva and abandon restraint!

definitions.meaning: Lady Godiva rode naked through Coventry covered only by her long loose tresses
an idiom for relaxing and enjoying oneself without inhibition

explanation.surface: Copy the legendary naked rider and throw off all inhibitions!
explanation.walkthrough: Lady Godiva is the English legend of a noblewoman who rode naked through Coventry, her flowing locks her only cover.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means to relax completely; literally it describes loosening bound tresses, as the legendary rider did.

clue.text: Leather made by husband in compound

indicators.note: the husband letter is put inside the compound word

parts.note: an oxide is a chemical compound of oxygen
H is the abbreviation for husband in genealogy

explanation.surface: Some leather has been produced by a man treating it with a chemical.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' puts H inside OXIDE.
explanation.definitionFit: The skin of a bullock, tanned, is a heavy kind of leather.

clue.text: Stout bag for one possessing wine

parts.note: a haver is one who has, a possessor
sack is an old name for a dry white wine from Spain

explanation.surface: A sturdy bag for someone who owns wine.
explanation.walkthrough: SACK is the sherry-like wine Falstaff loved.
explanation.definitionFit: A haversack is a strong canvas bag carried on the back or shoulder.

clue.text: Father's attempts to make cakes

parts.note: pa is a familiar word for father, with the possessive S
tries are attempts

explanation.surface: Dad has a go at baking some cakes.
explanation.definitionFit: Pastries are small baked goods, so a cake is a fair loose synonym.

clue.text: Story concealed by second officer in no-win situation

indicators.note: the story word is hidden inside the second and officer pieces

parts.note: a mate is an officer on a merchant ship
a tale is a story

explanation.surface: A tale kept secret by a ship's deputy leads to deadlock.
explanation.walkthrough: 'concealed by' means the story is hidden inside the officer phrase, which here is a ship's officer, not a military one.
explanation.definitionFit: In chess, a position with no legal move and no check ends as a draw; figuratively, a deadlock.

clue.text: Hothead pinches wood in malice

indicators.note: the malice word nips the wood word between its letters, holding it inside

parts.note: spite is malice
fir is a softwood timber

explanation.surface: A hot-tempered person spitefully filches timber.
explanation.walkthrough: 'pinches' is the container signal: malice nips the timber inside itself; 'in' is a link saying where the wood goes.
explanation.definitionFit: A spitfire is a fiery-tempered person, quick to anger.

clue.text: It may bear the stamp of a first-class writer

definitions.text: It may bear the stamp of a first-class writer

parts.words: It may bear the stamp of a first-class writer
parts.note: reads as praise of a great author's style, but means paper cover carrying a postage stamp, sent first-class post by whoever wrote the letter

explanation.walkthrough: 'stamp' and 'first-class' suggest literary merit; they are postal: British mail goes first or second class.
explanation.definitionFit: A letter's paper cover carries the postage stamp, and first-class is a British postal rate.

clue.text: Carelessly tear old acrobat's gear

explanation.surface: An old acrobat's costume gets ripped through neglect.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Carelessly' rearranges TEAROLD.
explanation.definitionFit: A leotard is the close-fitting one-piece garment worn by gymnasts and dancers.

clue.text: Equipment for shooting arrived before gunners

indicators.note: the arrived piece comes before the gunners piece

parts.note: came means arrived

clue.text: Loving a type of sherry mostly found round university

indicators.note: the shortened sherry word is placed around the university letter

parts.note: amoroso is a sweet dark style of sherry

clue.text: Reportedly travels around selling bicycle parts

parts.note: a hawker peddles, going from place to place selling goods

explanation.surface: Word is a hawker deals in bike components.

clue.text: A little salmon announced as part of meal, as usual

explanation.walkthrough: 'announced' turns FOURTH COURSE into the sound-alike FOR THE COURSE.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means what is normal or expected, from golf's standard score for a round.

clue.text: Supporter of current conductor gets piano for 8's opening

clue.text: Some recall a majestic beast

clue.text: Appearance of first characters before apron stage
